name: Afcom Holdings Ltd
tagline: Only pure-play Indian scheduled air-cargo airline riding a Red Sea sea-to-air shift -- excellent returns and a fresh trusted thesis, but FY26 EBITDA margin (~40%) is at a cyclical peak, sequential momentum has rolled over, and the Q1 FY27 concall softened the Boeing 777 wide-body plan to 'no firm plan at this stage'
business_overview: Afcom Holdings operates air freight/charter cargo services covering e-commerce, mobile phones, and seafood shipments, domestic and international, and is affiliated with sister company FlySBS (private charter jets) under the same promoter group.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 4,483 Cr (price ~Rs 1,561, Aug-26); P/E ~30x; EPS FY26 Rs 46.76
Revenue Rs 583 Cr (+144%); EBITDA Rs 234 Cr (40% OPM); PAT Rs 122 Cr (+230%) -- executed mostly on 2 aircraft
Revenue Rs 176 Cr (+48% YoY, -7% QoQ vs Rs 190 Cr Q4); PAT Rs 39.2 Cr (+86% YoY, -12% QoQ); EPS Rs 14.16
OPM 22-24% (FY23-24) -> 29% (FY25) -> 40-47% (recent quarters) -- elevated by Red Sea charter premium
Rs 18 Cr (FY24) -> Rs 26 Cr (FY25) -> Rs 401 Cr (FY26) -- aircraft + lease liabilities from the dry-lease model shift; interest ~Rs 9.9 Cr/qtr
FY26 CFO Rs 36 Cr vs PAT Rs 122 Cr (~30%) -- down from 124% (FY24) / 56% (FY25); Q1 FY27 CFO Rs 52 Cr better
3x Boeing 737-800 freighters; target 5 by end-FY27; ~11 hrs/day utilisation
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely high-quality small/mid-cap: ~33% ROCE/ROE, five-year profit CAGR near 100%, and the only pure-play Indian scheduled air-cargo airline, with hazmat (classes 1-9) permits and a point-to-point model. FY26 revenue Rs 583 Cr (+144%), PAT Rs 122 Cr (+230%). But the deep read adds three cautions: (1) the ~40% EBITDA margin is a cyclical peak -- through FY23-FY25 it ran 22-29%; the lift is Red Sea shipping disruption driving a sea-to-air shift and charter premium, which management and independent analysts expect to normalise; (2) sequential momentum has rolled over -- revenue and PAT both fell QoQ in Q1 FY27 even as YoY stayed strong, and the YoY rate has decelerated from +144% (FY26) to +48%; (3) cash conversion is weak -- FY26 CFO only Rs 36 Cr against Rs 122 Cr PAT -- and borrowings/lease liabilities jumped to ~Rs 401 Cr with the dry-lease model shift. The Boeing 777 wide-body step-change the bull case leaned on was softened in the Q1 FY27 concall to 'no firm plan at this stage'.
technical_read: Not pulled. 52-week range Rs 638 - Rs 1,587; trading near the top of the range.

verdict_headline: Excellent-quality air-cargo operator with a real structural tailwind and a fresh trusted thesis -- but FY26 margins are a cyclical peak, sequential momentum has rolled over, cash conversion is weak, and the 777 wide-body step-change was walked back in the Q1 FY27 concall; conviction cut to Medium
verdict_reasoning: The business quality is genuine (33% ROCE/ROE, structural sea-to-air shift, only pure-play Indian scheduled cargo airline) and there is a live 3->5 narrowbody fleet catalyst -- keeps the growth-bucket thesis, tagged contingent

Conviction lowered Medium-High -> Medium: the ~40% EBITDA margin is well above the 22-29% FY23-FY25 through-cycle band and is Red Sea-cyclical; revenue and PAT both fell QoQ in Q1 FY27; FY26 cash conversion was ~30% of PAT; borrowings/lease liabilities rose to ~Rs 401 Cr; and the Boeing 777 induction -- the crux of the earlier 'underestimated' call -- was softened to 'no firm plan at this stage'

No red-flag tier. Watch: H2 FY27 prints for whether the ~40% margin holds as disruption normalises; a firm 777 decision (or not); fleet reaching 5 narrowbody; Singapore/SE Asia route approvals; and whether cash conversion recovers
